notes:
HOW THIS FILE WAS BUILT. Web search stopped partway through (the shared search allowance ran out), so most of the work was done by reading pages directly: company pages, state and local economic development pages, the EPA Facility Registry Service (FRS), and Wikipedia city articles that quote city annual financial reports. Printing and furniture are thin for that reason, and several leads could not be followed. Nothing was estimated.

COORDINATES. Each point is one of: the contract's geocode helper when it matched the house number in the right city; an OpenStreetMap feature carrying the plant's name; or the EPA FRS record for the plant. The helper's street-only matches were not used: on long highways they were kilometres out (Nucor Jewett, Optimus Steel, Sabre Alvarado). Points taken from FRS alone, without a second match: Steel Dynamics Sinton, Tenaris Bay City, Tenaris Baytown, Wyman-Gordon Houston, Hunter Cement, Acme Brick Denton and Malakoff, Georgia-Pacific Diboll, Pineland, Sweetwater and Quanah, West Fraser New Boston, LP Carthage, Clayton Bonham, Cavco Seguin, Graphic Packaging Waco, International Paper Orange, Nucor Longview.

HEADCOUNTS. 30 of the 89 plants carry a figure (two more are whole-state or whole-company figures on the company). Three kinds need a reviewer's eye. (1) "Texas Enterprise Zone" figures (Howmet Wichita Falls, Kiewit, Sabre, W&W|AFCO, Ball, Cemex, Vitro, Guardian, Owens Corning, Johns Manville, James Hardie Waxahachie, Kohler, Georgia-Pacific, Smurfit Westrock, Kimberly-Clark, Madix) are the jobs on site when the state approved the project, 2015 to 2020, read on texans.pages.dev, a third-party copy of the state's records; the Governor's office record was not opened. (2) Figures from city annual financial reports were read on Wikipedia, not in the reports (Gerdau, Graphic Packaging Texarkana, Clayton Sulphur Springs, Champion Burleson, Western Extrusions). (3) Undated company or EDC pages are given the year they were read, 2026 (CMC Seguin, Wyman-Gordon, and the state totals for Georgia-Pacific and Artcobell).

CONFLICTS. CMC Seguin: 900 (EDC list) against 500 (state record, 2018) and "approximately 1,000 direct jobs" in press coverage not opened. Vitro Wichita Falls: 330 (state, 2018) against 934 (Chamber list, undated). Gerdau Midlothian: the city lists 1,250 as the top of a band; a Gerdau job posting seen only in a search summary said about 1,030 for the mill and its downstream sites. Kiewit Ingleside: a Kiewit job posting seen only in a search summary describes about 300 staff and 1,400 craft workers.

OPERATING STATUS NOT RE-CONFIRMED ONLINE. These are listed as operating on the strength of a current EPA registry record and general knowledge, not a page read this session: Howmet Fastening Systems Waco, Ellwood Texas Forge Houston, Simpson Strong-Tie McKinney, USG Sweetwater and Galena Park, National Gypsum Rotan, O-I Waco, Georgia-Pacific Sweetwater and Quanah gypsum, the five West Fraser mills, LP Carthage and Jasper, Clayton Bonham and Waco, Cavco Seguin and Fort Worth, Legacy Housing Fort Worth and Commerce, Graphic Packaging Waco (a new mill planned to start in late 2025), Johns Manville and James Hardie Cleburne, American Leather Dallas, Mueller Ballinger, Hensley Dallas. The Acme Brick plant list is from an unsourced section of Wikipedia's Acme Brick article, which marks Bridgeport, Garrison and McQueeney as closed.

JUDGMENT CALLS. Kiewit Offshore Services is a steel fabrication yard and is filed under Fabricated Metal. Howmet's Wichita Falls casting plant is filed under Primary Metal (foundry) and its Waco fastener plant under Fabricated Metal. Kimberly-Clark Paris (diapers) is Paper Manufacturing by NAICS. The Bureau of Engraving and Printing is a federal agency, included because its Fort Worth plant is the largest printing site found. ASARCO Amarillo is listed as operating because a 2024 union agreement covers its workers, but reports that year spoke of restarting the refinery, so part of it may be idle; a local radio report from the 2019 strike gave 244 hourly and 94 salaried workers. Cavco is shown as the owner of the Oak Creek Homes (American Homestar) plants because the EPA registry now carries them as "Cavco - Lancaster" and "Cavco - Lake Arlington"; the purchase itself was not read on a page. Amrize is Holcim's former North American business (holcim.us now opens as Amrize); the cement association's May 2025 sheet still says Holcim. Ash Grove's Hunter plant was Martin Marietta's (TXI) until 2024. Georgia-Pacific's two gypsum plants are under Georgia-Pacific with the Nonmetallic Mineral subsector.

NAMES ALREADY IN THE DATABASE. "Txi" is Texas Industries, part of Martin Marietta since 2014: cement at Midlothian plus ready-mix and aggregates sites (the Hunter cement plant went to Ash Grove/CRH). "Campbell Soup" under minerals is most likely Campbell Concrete & Materials, a Houston ready-mix concrete firm that became part of Cemex, and has nothing to do with the food company; this was not confirmed on a page, so it is not in Cemex's alsoKnownAs. "Lattimore Materials" is a North Texas ready-mix and aggregates firm bought by Holcim's Aggregate Industries in 2011 (now Amrize), also unconfirmed here and left out of alsoKnownAs. Ready-mix plants are small (a handful of people each) and none are listed. "Alcoa": its Point Comfort and Rockdale operations are shut; no operating Alcoa plant was found in Texas. "Trinity Industries": its Texas plants build rail cars (Transportation Equipment); the tank, tower and highway-product businesses once filed under fabricated metal were spun off as Arcosa in 2018, and no Arcosa fabricating plant in Texas was confirmed. "Oldcastle" is CRH: concrete products (Oldcastle APG, Oldcastle Infrastructure) and glass (Oldcastle BuildingEnvelope), not wood. "Louisiana-Pacific" has many old sawmill and panel sites in East Texas in government lists (Silsbee, Cleveland, Corrigan, Bon Wier, New Waverly); only Carthage and Jasper are listed here. "International Paper": the Orange containerboard mill is marked closed (announced in late 2023) and the Texarkana mill is now Graphic Packaging's; both facts are from the researcher's own knowledge plus the registry names, not from a page read this session, and the same goes for the closure year of Nucor Longview, which rests on a search summary of a Recycling Today report and a June 2023 layoff notice; its many box plants, and Packaging Corporation of America's, were not researched. "Leggett & Platt" has EPA registry records in Ennis, Fort Worth and Brenham that were not confirmed. The loader should not merge "Lone Star Industries" rows blindly into Buzzi Unicem: some old records under that name are closed terminals.

LEFT OUT, WITH WHAT IS KNOWN. Not confirmed as operating or not researched for lack of search: U.S. Steel Lone Star Tubular Operations (6866 US 259 S, Lone Star; idled, status unknown), TPCO America (5431 Highway 35, Gregory; its own site still describes a ramp-up), Borusan pipe mill (4949 Borusan Rd, Baytown), Vallourec Star (8603 Sheldon Rd, Houston), Kaiser Aluminum (Sherman), Texarkana Aluminum (300 Alumax Rd), Ball Conroe (1001 N FM 3083 Rd E), Hudson Products (Chart Industries; 9660 Grunwald Rd, Beasley), Valmont Newmark (Bellville), Flowserve Sulphur Springs (below the city's top-ten cut of 183 employees in 2024), Owens Corning Amarillo (1701 Hollywood Rd; a glass reinforcements plant, a business Owens Corning was selling), Dal-Tile (El Paso, Sunnyvale, Dallas), Knauf Insulation (McGregor), Lehigh White Cement (Woodway), Georgia-Pacific Diboll particleboard and Corrigan plywood (the state recorded 374 jobs at Corrigan in December 2015), Clayton Athens, Champion Athens, Palm Harbor (Austin, Fort Worth), Fleetwood Waco, Republic Elite (Marshall), Corsicana Mattress, Ashley Furniture (Mesquite), Harland Clarke (San Antonio), RR Donnelley and Quad sites. Weyerhaeuser: no Texas mill was found. Encore Wire (McKinney), Emerson and Cameron valve plants, General Dynamics ordnance plants (Garland, Mesquite) and Priefert (Mount Pleasant) sit on the border of these industries and were left to the electrical, machinery and defence briefs.

V2, OSHA PASS (18 November 2026). Headcounts that were missing have been filled from OSHA's Form 300A establishment data (https://www.osha.gov/Establishment-Specific-Injury-and-Illness-Data): the files for reporting year 2025 and, where an establishment has no 2025 row, 2024, read from the copies on disk. The figure is the establishment's own 'annual average number of employees': that employer's people at that address, offices on the site included, contractors not included. A row was taken only when it had the same street address in the same city, or the same ZIP code and a name that is plainly this plant; each employeesNote names the row. Contractors' filings from the same address (maintenance, scaffolding, catering, security) were never used. Nothing else was changed except as listed here. Web search was not available, so nothing in this pass was checked against a company page. SCOPE RULE (construction is not manufacturing: no ready-mix, concrete block, pipe or precast, NAICS 3273, and no asphalt paving mixtures, 324121): no plant in this file is one of those, so none was removed. COUNTS: 40 plants filled (38 from the 2025 file, 2 from 2024); 19 still without a figure; 11 existing figures annotated with a differing OSHA figure; 70 of 89 plants now carry a headcount. OPERATING STATUS: for 27 plants that the earlier research could not confirm as operating, the note now says that a filing from the address is good evidence it was operating that year (OSHA's page is added to the plant's sources). SCOPE JUDGMENT FOR THE OWNER. The ten cement plants (NAICS 327310: Martin Marietta, Amrize and Ash Grove at Midlothian, Ash Grove Hunter, Cemex Balcones, Buzzi Maryneal and San Antonio, Capitol, GCC Odessa, Texas Lehigh Buda) and the two James Hardie fiber-cement plants (327390) were KEPT. The rule names ready-mix, block, pipe and precast; cement kilns and siding factories are none of those, but their codes sit inside NAICS 3273, so if the owner meant the whole group these twelve are the ones to drop. CEMENT PLANTS HAVE NO OSHA FIGURE: quarries and cement plants report to the mine safety agency (MSHA), not OSHA, so the nine without a headcount stay without one. NOT FOUND: ASARCO Amarillo, O-I Waco (a 2024 row shows 24 people, which cannot be a working glass plant, and there is no 2025 row), Georgia-Pacific Acme Wallboard (Quanah), West Fraser Lufkin and Nacogdoches, Graphic Packaging Waco (the only filing at the address is a construction contractor's, 945 people in 2025, which fits a mill still being built), Leedo Cabinetry. KENT MOORE CABINETS: the listed address, 501 Industrial Blvd, files as the corporate office (62 people); the plants file from 1460 Fountain Ave (196) and 350 Stone City Dr (239), so no figure was put on the listed plant. JUDGMENT CALLS IN MATCHING: Georgia-Pacific Sweetwater is the sum of the east and west plants, which file separately from 311 and 310 FM 1856 (148 + 107); Georgia-Pacific files under site codes with no company name ('TX026 Sweetwater Gypsum EAST'). National Gypsum Rotan files as 'Gold Bond Building Products'. Acme Brick's plants file with the company name given as 'Production'. Mueller Ballinger's 2025 filing is 'Metal Solutions - Ballinger' at the same address (238; 307 as Mueller in 2024). Simpson Strong-Tie files from 2151 Airport Drive and Tenaris Baytown from 2600 Grand Parkway, the same sites under other street names. Freeport-McMoRan El Paso (197) files as Phelps Dodge Industries under a copper wire code and may be the rod mill only. COMPARISONS added to notes (figure left alone): Steel Dynamics Sinton (600 against 973), CMC Seguin (900 against 665), Wyman-Gordon (669 against 263), Kiewit Ingleside (1,365 against 2,172), Valmont Brenham, Guardian Corsicana, Johns Manville Cleburne, James Hardie Waxahachie, Kohler Brownwood (900 against 506 for its two filings), Georgia-Pacific Pineland, Champion Burleson. Vitro Wichita Falls, Kimberly-Clark Paris, Cemex and JSW (598, within a fifth) have no usable row or agree.
